title: In affine chains, persistence and composition across time are decided by two row sequences of M^T
subject: Reducing the contact-network gate across time, on affine chains of three rings, to linear recurring sequences over GF(2)
conclusion: For three-ring chains with linear or affine rules and affine contact laws, a contact's value at lag T is the parity of the first-row cells in its row of M^T plus a constant, so it binds two rings exactly when that row meets both, and the chain composes when the far contact's row meets both end rings. The rows are eventually periodic, so iterating them until they repeat decides every lag exactly.
